title: Publication of people’s real-time geolocation data under Spain’s compulsory V16 system
text:
QUESTION

PE780.976v01-00
Question for written answer E-000006/2026
to the Commission
Rule 144
Alvise Pérez (NI)
Subject:
Publication of people’s real-time geolocation data under Spain’s compulsory V16
system
Spanish legislation requires the use of connected V16 devices to indicate vehicles that have
broken down or are stopped on the public highway. The devices also transmit geolocation
data to systems managed by the Directorate-General for Traffic.
Real-time location information is publicly available on a web-based map – access is
unrestricted and no login is required. As a result, anyone can look up the location of people
who find themselves in potentially vulnerable situations.
While national authorities argue that data is ‘anonymised’, exact and real-time geolocation
can constitute personal data when it indirectly enables natural persons to be identified or
poses a risk to their safety.
In light of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (General Data Protection Regulation):
1.
Does the Commission believe that a Member State making real-time geolocation
information provided under a mandatory system is consistent with the GDPR?
2.
Is the mere claim of anonymisation enough, when the precise nature of the data
indirectly allows a person to be identified or could generate risks?
3.
Would such processing necessarily require a data protection impact assessment and
restriction of access strictly to competent authorities? Does the Commission intend to
request information from the Spanish authorities regarding the applicable legal basis
and safeguards?
Submitted: 5.1.2026
